title: Thyroid hormones treatment for subclinical hypothyroidism: a clinical practice guideline
authors: Bekkering GE, Agoritsas T, Lytvyn L, Heen AF, Feller M, Moutzouri E, et al.
authorConflicts: The BMJ Rapid Recommendations executive team and The BMJ judged that no panel member had any relevant financial conflict of interest. M Feller, M Snel, E Moutzouri and N Rodondi wrote the systematic review on which the guideline rests; JP Brito and N Singh Ospina wrote an editorial about the overuse of levothyroxine.
result: BMJ Rapid Recommendation (MAGIC group, GRADE): strong recommendation against thyroid hormones for adults with subclinical hypothyroidism (raised TSH, normal free T4). Not applicable to women trying to become pregnant or to TSH above 20 mIU/l; may not apply to severe symptoms or adults aged 30 or under. Based on a systematic review of 21 trials with 2192 participants: no clinically relevant benefit for quality of life or thyroid-related symptoms (moderate to high quality evidence). Deaths at 2 years 14 against 27 per 1000 without and with thyroid hormones (95% CI 5 fewer to 62 more per 1000; low quality, one trial). The evidence addresses starting treatment and only indirectly informs stopping it.
